title: Weld an L-shaped seam with a TIG torch and filler rod
instruction: Weld the joint between the white and yellow marks with the TIG torch, dabbing the yellow filler rod into the front of the pool to lay one sound bead, then put both tools back on their rests and move both hands away.
context: Manual TIG (GTAW) welding is a core fabrication trade skill with a persistent shortage of welders. It takes two hands at once: one carries the torch along the joint at a steady 2-5 mm arc length, and the other dabs filler rod into the front of the pool and withdraws it, so that neither the rod nor the plate ever touches the tungsten, which would contaminate it and stop the weld.
setup: A steel fixture-table top (29 x 27 cm, 12 mm thick, dark grey, a 50 mm hole grid; x 11.5 to 40.5 cm, y -13.5 to 13.5 cm) on the station table. On it, two 6 mm mild-steel plates, held by three blue strap clamps, meet in an L-shaped butt joint with 45 degree bevels 2 mm deep each side (a 4 mm V, dark root line): an inner plate (15 x 11 cm, x 19.5 to 34.5, y -9 to 2 cm) and an L-shaped plate around it (x 14.5 to 34.5, y 2 to 7 cm, plus x 14.5 to 19.5, y -9 to 2 cm). The joint runs 12 cm along -x from the start (31.5, 2) cm to the corner (19.5, 2) cm, then 8 cm along -y to the end (19.5, -6) cm: 200 mm in all. A white paint mark (6 x 30 mm) is beside the start and a yellow one (30 x 6 mm) beside the end. The TIG torch (255 g) lies on two steel rest posts (45 mm tall) on a steel base, its glass-filled nylon grip block (30 x 36 x 26 mm, orange) centred at (20, 21) cm: a 22 mm rubber-covered handle 11 cm long with a 4 cm stub of power cable behind it, a black head 24 mm across with its axis 17.5 degrees from vertical, a pink ceramic cup (14 to 18 mm across, 25 mm long) and a 2.4 mm tungsten sticking out 5 mm, pointing along -x. The filler rod is a 3.2 mm steel rod painted yellow, leaving the underside of a 25 mm blue nylon grip sleeve (white band) sloping 20 degrees down, its tip 21.25 cm from the sleeve's centre along the rod (32 g in all); the sleeve sits on a steel post at (12, -25) cm, the rod along +x, its tip on a 3 mm black rubber pad. Positions are from the arm bases' midpoint in x and the table's centre line in y, with +y toward the left arm. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: Read at the end of the run. The 200 mm joint is scored in 40 segments of 5 mm. A hand is a gripper's fingertip midpoint; a hand holds a tool when it is within 2.5 cm of the tool's grip block or sleeve centre. The arc is on while the torch is held, its tungsten tip is 2-5 mm above the plates and within 4 mm (in plan) of the joint line (the line extended 5 mm past each mark). While the arc is on, every segment whose centre is within 8 mm of the tip gains that time: it is molten while under the arc with 0.5 s or more, fused at 3 s, and burnt through at 9 s. A dab is the rod tip (the centre of its end), in the hand not holding the torch, coming within 3.5 mm of the plates after being lifted 6 mm or more; it counts if the arc is on and the rod tip is 3-10 mm ahead of the tungsten tip along the torch's lean (its push direction) and within 4 mm of the joint line, and it gives each molten segment within 6 mm of the rod tip one dab of filler. A segment is sound with at least one dab of filler and 3 to 9 s of arc, not burnt through. Contamination, latched for the rest of the run: the tungsten tip within 0.5 mm of the plates' top (or below it) anywhere over the fixture table, or the rod within 0.5 mm of the tungsten (their axes 3.3 mm apart); from then on there is no arc. 0 if the torch or the rod falls off the table. Otherwise 0.9 x the fraction of the 40 segments that are sound (rounded to 0.001), capped at 0.5 after contamination or any burn-through. 1.0 with all 40 segments sound, no contamination or burn-through, both tools back on their rests (each grip centre within 12 mm in plan and 6 mm in height of its rest position, tilted under 10 degrees, turned under 20 degrees), both hands 6 cm or more from every part of both tools, and both tools at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) with the hands clear for the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the torch back on its rest posts and the rod's sleeve back on its post with the tip on the pad. Nothing is consumed: the plates are unchanged, since the bead is a record of the trial, not deposited metal, and it is cleared at reset.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with real contact for the torch, rod, plates and hands; the plates are flat colliders (the bevels are drawn) and the strap clamps are drawn only. The arc, heat and filler are not physically simulated. The arc is a geometric condition (tungsten height above the plates and distance from the joint), heat is the time a segment spends within 8 mm of the tungsten under the arc, and a dab of filler is a counted event; nothing melts, flows, distorts or is deposited, and the rod doesn't get shorter. There is no current, pedal, shielding gas or torch hose drag (the cable is a 4 cm stub). The bead, pool and arc glow are shown from the score's record. Contamination is geometric: any touch of the tungsten counts, as it would on a real torch.
